title: FDA exemptions and deferrals of Medication Guide content and format requirements
subtopic: Content and format exemptions under 21 CFR 208.26(a)
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 208.26(a) FDA, on its own initiative or in response to a written request from an applicant, may exempt or defer any Medication Guide content or format requirement, except the requirements in 21 CFR 208.20(a)(2) and (a)(6), on the basis that the requirement is inapplicable, unnecessary, or contrary to patients' best interests. Requests from applicants should be submitted to the director of the FDA division responsible for reviewing the marketing application for the drug product, or for a biological product to the application division in the office with product responsibility. Section 208.20(a)(2) requires a Medication Guide to be scientifically accurate and to be based on, and not conflict with, the approved professional labeling for the drug product, although its language need not be identical to the corresponding sections of the approved labeling. Section 208.20(a)(6) requires the words "Medication Guide" to appear prominently at the top of the first page and the verbatim statement "This Medication Guide has been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration" to appear at the bottom.
exam_relevance: Tests who holds the exemption power in 21 CFR 208.26(a) and what it reaches: FDA, acting on its own initiative or on an applicant's written request, and the content or format requirements of the Guide itself.

authority.name: Content and format of a Medication Guide

exceptions: The requirements in 21 CFR 208.20(a)(2) and (a)(6) may not be exempted or deferred under 21 CFR 208.26(a).
common_confusions: Reading 21 CFR 208.26(a) as an exemption a pharmacist may apply at the counter; it authorizes FDA, on its own initiative or on an applicant's written request, to exempt or defer content or format requirements.
Treating scientific accuracy and consistency with approved labeling, or the required title and FDA-approval statement, as requirements FDA may waive under 21 CFR 208.26(a); both are excluded.
